title: Designing Teaching Materials with GenAI: Perceptions of Cognitive Load and Learner Competencies in Higher Education
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly used to design instructional materials in higher education, yet limited evidence exists on students’ perceptions of the cognitive demands and learner-related competencies involved. Drawing on Cognitive Load Theory, this study examined university students’ perceptions of GenAI-supported instructional material design according to gender, age, and admission grade. A quantitative, non-experimental, ex post facto study was conducted with 451 university students enrolled in education-related undergraduate and master’s programmes. The instrument assessed perceived usefulness, beliefs concerning metacognitive practices, prior knowledge, and problem-solving strategies, and perceived intrinsic, extraneous, and germane cognitive load. Participants generally reported positive perceptions. Female students reported significantly higher scores on the metacognitive skills, prior knowledge, and problem-solving skills dimensions, although effect sizes were small. title: Chinese Preschool Educators’ Perspectives on Play-Based Learning and Its Relationships with Their Language Use in Free and Structured Play Contexts
abstract: The pedagogical value of play-based learning is well established, yet its effectiveness depends on contextual factors such as play type, educators’ perspectives, and their language use. In the background of China’s curriculum transformation, this study examines 28 early childhood educators’ perspectives on play-based learning and their language use during free and structured play. Interviews identified two perspectives on the relationship between play and learning: interdependent (19) and independent (9). Drawing on systemic functional linguistics, educators’ speech functions were analyzed in terms of how speakers give or demand information and goods & services, expressed through statement, question, command, and offer. Findings showed that language use differed across play contexts: while offers were rare in both, free play featured a balanced use of statements, questions, and commands, whereas structured play was marked by a greater use of statements and commands. title: Humanizing the Asynchronous Classroom: A Framework for Authentic Online Learning
abstract: Designing asynchronous courses involves attention to students’ relationships, goals, access, and opportunities to contribute to shared learning. This practitioner-focused conceptual article proposes the Authentic Asynchronous Classroom Framework (AACF), informed by relevant literature and two instructors’ experiences redesigning and teaching asynchronous teacher-preparation courses at different universities. A grant-supported, comprehensive course redesign and a multi-year course redesign provided the contexts for reflection and framework development. The AACF organizes humanizing course-design practices into four tiers: Radical Instructor Presence, Student-Centered Utility, Universal and Equitable Design, and Reciprocal Co-Creation. The tier order reflects the instructors’ perceptions of implementation time and effort. Practices may support more than one tier, and instructors can address multiple tiers concurrently. Course examples illustrate responsive feedback, assignments with practical applications, attention to material costs and accessibility, and student contributions to course content and shared resources. title: Generative AI and Digital Inequality in South African Higher Education: Students’ Experiences of Access and Meaningful Use at a Rural University
abstract: This study examined the conditions that enable or constrain undergraduate students’ access to, and meaningful use of, generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) at a rural South African university. Using an interpretivist qualitative case study design, researchers conducted semi-structured, face-to-face interviews with 12 undergraduate students with prior experience using GenAI for academic purposes. Data were analysed thematically following Braun and Clarke’s ix-phase approach. Four interconnected conditions shaped students’ experiences: device and connectivity reliability, the affordability of sustained data access, artificial intelligence (AI) literacy, and institutional infrastructure and training. Students consistently perceived GenAI as useful, but their capacity to realise that usefulness depended on resources and competencies that were unevenly distributed. The study uses this gap to extend TAM’s construct of perceived usefulness with a distinct construct of realised usefulness, and this study argues that generative AI introduces a literacy demand, critical evaluation of machine-generated, plausible-sounding but sometimes inaccurate output. title: Career Outcomes, Experiences, and Transition Programs for Postsecondary Students with Disabilities: A Review of the Literature from 2013 to 2025
abstract: As more students with disabilities access postsecondary education, it is important for the field to understand their post-graduation employment outcomes. A systematic literature review using preferred reporting items for systematic reviews and meta-analyses (PRISMA) guidelines was conducted related to the employment outcomes of students with disabilities from the peer-reviewed literature published in English from 2013 to 2025. A total of 104 articles were reviewed and were grouped into categories related to employment outcomes, employment experiences, and career-focused interventions. Results indicated students with disabilities who access postsecondary education have higher levels of employment and earnings than peers with disabilities who do not access postsecondary education, that they report facing discrimination and accessibility issues in the workplace, and that programs such as mentoring and internships show promise in promoting access to employment.

title: Learning Sciences Foundations for Engineering Education: A Framework for Epistemological Articulation Across Paradigms
abstract: Educational research explains learning through three major traditions—behaviorism, cognitivism, and the situative perspective—yet typically deploys them as rival options rather than complementary levels of analysis. This article argues that the fragmentation is not a matter of preference but an unresolved epistemological problem: the three paradigms operate on qualitatively distinct epistemic objects—observable behavior, the internal architecture of knowledge and its acquisition and transfer, and the structurally distributed conditions that determine what counts as knowing in a disciplinary community—and therefore generate questions, instruments, and validity criteria that are not mutually substitutable. On this basis, we develop a conceptual synthesis that does not unify the paradigms but specifies the conditions under which each—together with its contemporary extensions (Cognitive Load Theory, self-regulated learning, Self-Determination Theory, and the Cognitive Theory of Multimedia Learning)—is methodologically productive. title: Digital Technologies in Undergraduate Dental Education: A Scoping Review
abstract: Digital technologies are becoming increasingly embedded in undergraduate dental curricula, with the potential to support learning and skills development. This scoping review mapped recent evidence on the implementation and educational applications of contemporary digital technologies in undergraduate dental education. A literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science to identify studies published between 2021 and 2025. The review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA-ScR reporting guidelines and included studies investigating digital technologies in undergraduate dental education. A total of 24 studies met the inclusion criteria. The identified technologies included virtual reality and simulation-based learning systems, digital and 3D-printed educational models, digital assessment and feedback systems, web-based learning platforms, artificial intelligence applications, CAD/CAM technologies, and digital clinical devices. title: Bridging the Computational Gap in the Social Sciences: Dual Innovations in Pedagogy and Assessment
abstract: In a world increasingly dominated by data, graduates in STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) fields are in high demand. This focus often obscures the fact that a significant portion of digital data is social in nature, generated through human–computer interactions. Consequently, experts trained in the social sciences should be equally sought after, yet this is not consistently the case. A contributing factor is the tendency for social and political science departments to adhere to traditional disciplinary boundaries, inadvertently marginalizing their graduates from a growing number of data-centric professions. This paper argues that this gap can and should be addressed. title: Effective Strategies for Learning Solving Well-Structured Problems in STEM Education: A Systematic Literature Review
abstract: Problem-solving is central to STEM in higher education, yet evidence on effective learning strategies for problem-solving remains fragmented across cognitive psychology and discipline-specific research. This systematic literature review, conducted following the PRISMA framework, identifies, categorizes, and analyzes empirical evidence for the learning of well-structured problems in STEM higher education. The strategies reviewed build on two established frameworks of desirably difficult and generative learning strategies. Across three databases (ERIC, PsycINFO, Web of Science), supplemented by citation tracking and screening with ASReview of over 11,000 records, 34 peer-reviewed empirical studies were retained. This review addresses which strategies improve problem-solving in STEM higher education, and how student characteristics, teacher support, and implementation factors shape their effectiveness; data were extracted thematically across these four dimensions. Results show that distributed practice, drawing, enacting, self-explanation, and testing improved problem-solving across STEM contexts. title: Practical Biophysics Education in Medical Schools in Türkiye and Northern Cyprus: A National Needs Assessment and a Proposed Modular Framework
abstract: Maintaining minimum shared learning outcomes in practice-based basic science education is challenging when institutions differ in academic staffing, student cohort size, and laboratory resources. Using practical biophysics education as a disciplinary case, this cross-sectional, multi-source study assessed how medical schools in Türkiye and the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus address these constraints and proposed a resource-adaptable modular framework. Official curriculum documents and a 16-item online survey were used. Invitations were sent to 86 medical schools; 40 departments responded and 38 provided analysable data, and verified curriculum data were available for 72. Practical education was identified in 39 schools (54.2%), while 37 (51.4%) had a laboratory. Among schools providing practical education, the median annual teaching time was 10 h. title: Broadening the Assessment of Mathematics-Related Achievement Emotions: Structure and Differentiation of an Extended AEQ-ES Among Chilean Elementary School Children
abstract: Achievement emotions play a central role in mathematics learning, yet instruments suitable for young children often cover only a narrow range of emotions and have rarely been validated in Latin American contexts. This study examined the structure, differentiation, and measurement properties of mathematics-related achievement emotions using an extended Spanish-language version of the Achievement Emotions Questionnaire–Elementary School (AEQ-ES). The instrument, referred to here as the AEQ-ES-M, was extended to include anger and hope, alongside the original dimensions of enjoyment, anxiety, and boredom. Items were translated and back-translated, and semantic equivalence was assessed using Sentence-BERT embeddings (cosine similarities = 0.70–0.96). A new set of facial icons depicting a boy or a girl was developed for all five emotions, and their recognizability was examined in an independent face-matching task with 399 second-graders (overall accuracy = 79.6%). title: Paper or Tablet? A Retrospective Study of Preference and Performance
abstract: There is an ongoing debate over whether paper or electronic media are more pedagogically effective for student learning. Existing research has indicated that handwriting may be more effective for notetaking than the use of a computer, but contradictory results have also been found. Since 2020, all incoming students on the Physics programmes at the University of Edinburgh have been provided with iPad devices. Thus, availability of electronic devices has been removed as a confounding factor, and we are able to investigate more clearly students’ preferences and any effect on their performance. We have conducted a study on these issues using a combination of a questionnaire and focus groups: we find a mix of student preferences between paper and electronic media that show indications of time-dependence, but no statistically significant effect on student performance.

title: Spatializing Racial Realism: Rural Latinx Youth and Postsecondary Opportunity in California’s San Joaquin Valley
abstract: Scholars have increasingly noted the importance of considering the intersections of race, rurality, and other social dimensions in research on college access and success. This article advances this intersectional line of inquiry in race-centered, rural higher education research by employing Bell’s theory of racial realism and Delaney’s concept of scale to understand the spatialization of racism in rural areas and its effects on racialized rural students’ postsecondary opportunities. This study employs Chicana/Latina feminist pláticas research methodology with rural Latinx high school seniors to examine the intersections among race, racism, place, and postsecondary opportunity in California’s San Joaquin Valley. Findings indicate that rural Latinx youth understood postsecondary opportunity as shaped by interconnected processes of residential and occupational racialization across local and regional contexts. title: Assessing Attitudes Toward Biophysics Content in University Health Education: A Colombian Sample
abstract: Medical students often perceive biophysics as irrelevant to clinical training. This study assessed first-year medical students’ attitudes toward biophysics using the Colorado Learning Attitudes about Science Survey (CLASS), with attention to gender differences. A cross-sectional survey was administered to 198 first-year medical students (110 women, 88 men) at a Colombian university during the biophysics course in 2018. Favourability scores were calculated for eight CLASS categories and analyzed by gender using Mann–Whitney U tests with 95% confidence intervals. Overall favourability was 49.0% (95% CI: [46.8%, 51.1%]), with no significant gender difference (U = 5213.5, p = 0.351, r = −0.08, 95% CI [−0.24, 0.09]). After Bonferroni correction (adjusted α = 0.0056), a significant gender difference was confirmed only in Personal Interest (men: 58.0%, women: 43.9%, p = 0.001). The difference in Real-World Connections (men: 64.2%, women: 54.3%, p = 0.048) did not survive correction. title: Integrating Language Growth Beliefs and Regulatory Experience: A Mixed-Methods Exploration of the Language Mindset and Regulation Inventory in a Thai EFL Setting
abstract: This mixed-methods study examined how language growth beliefs and related regulatory and emotional processes were represented in the Language Mindset and Regulation Inventory (LMRI) and explained in Thai undergraduate learners’ accounts of English learning. A quantitatively driven embedded survey design was used. The quantitative strand comprised 1565 complete responses to 21 six-point LMRI items, while the qualitative strand comprised responses to five open-ended prompts. Principal component analysis with Promax rotation identified three provisional components explaining 69.0% of the total variance: Growth Language Beliefs, Self-Regulated Language Resilience, and Language Confidence Under Challenge. Reflexive thematic analysis generated five themes: growth-oriented beliefs amid present limitations, purposeful goals and progress regulation, mistakes and feedback as resources for improvement, managing emotions to sustain participation, and contextual challenges and sources of support. title: Peer-Supported Learning in the Digital Transformation of Higher Education: A Theory-Informed Systematic Review
abstract: Peer support in higher education settings plays an important role in fostering collaboration, motivation, and resilience among learners in higher education. Higher education has undergone a rapid and sustained shift toward digital learning spaces, a transformation that the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated and that continues to expand with the growing integration of online, hybrid, and AI-enabled learning technologies. This systematic review synthesised evidence on peer-supported learning interventions and their association with academic performance, engagement, well-being, and professional development among higher education students in online and hybrid learning environments. A comprehensive literature search of PubMed, ERIC, and Web of Science, supplemented by Google Scholar, identified 19 eligible studies published between January 2020 and December 2024, a period spanning the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic and its aftermath. title: Toward Controllable Learner Simulation for Teacher Education: Benchmarking Skill-Profile Control in LLM Answer Behavior
abstract: Teacher preparation depends on deliberate practice with learners who have identifiable strengths and weaknesses, yet classroom experience accumulates slowly and is hard to standardize. Language-model-simulated students could offer scalable, repeatable practice, but only if a simulated learner can exhibit a specified answer-performance profile rather than behaving as a uniformly capable assistant. title: The Role of Social–Emotional Learning in Special and Inclusive Education: A Path Analysis Integrating Intrinsic Motivation, Efficacy, Stress, and Well-Being
abstract: Teaching in special and inclusive education presents unique emotional and ecological demands, yet the specific psychological mechanisms through which social–emotional learning (SEL) competencies relate to how teachers navigate these challenges remain underexplored. Therefore, the present study investigates the pathways linking educators’ SEL and intrinsic motivation to their psychological well-being. In this cross-sectional study, 459 educators completed self-report questionnaires assessing their SEL competencies, intrinsic motivation, teacher self-efficacy, perceived work stress, and psychological well-being. The findings show that both SEL competencies and intrinsic motivation are positively associated with teacher self-efficacy, which in turn is negatively related to perceived work stress and positively associated with psychological well-being. title: Trust of Pre-Service Teachers in Government Response to Gen AI Generated Deepfakes
abstract: This study examined the perceptions of pre-service teachers regarding the Spanish government’s response to the misuse of generative artificial intelligence (generative AI) for creating disinformation, as well as the mitigation of risks associated with deepfakes produced using these digital tools. A quantitative methodology was employed, involving 133 pre-service teachers pursuing a Primary Education degree in the Region of Murcia (Spain) who participated voluntarily. The results revealed low levels of confidence in the government’s response to these online threats. However, a minority of participants expressed greater confidence in the government and focused more on the risk of generative AI being misused to amplify manipulative disinformation campaigns. title: Modeling Relationships Among Classroom Environment, Motivation, and Creativity in Secondary Students’ Digital Music Compositions
abstract: Technology-based music classrooms differ structurally from traditional, teacher-directed settings, where self-paced, individualized composition with digital audio workstations may change how classroom environment and motivation relate to students’ creative output. Research on compositional creativity has rarely modeled these two factors together, and even less often in technology-mediated, self-paced contexts. This study tested a theoretical model examining the relationships among the classroom environment, motivation, and creativity of secondary students’ digital music compositions. High school students (N = 146) enrolled in technology-based music courses completed self-report measures of motivation and classroom environment and produced a digital composition in GarageBand as a self-paced compositional task without teacher-paced instruction. title: Evaluating Lesson Methodology Among Pre-Service Geography Teachers: A Repeated Cross-Sectional Study Based on a University Mentor’s Records
abstract: The integration of school-based practice remains central to preparing pre-service geography teachers (PSTs) for the classroom. This study examines how PSTs at the University of Niš (Serbia) applied teaching methods and classroom organization formats over a nine-year period, using the same evaluation instrument and research procedure with successive generations of PSTs, while also considering the role of university and school-based mentors within the teaching practicum. Based on university evaluators’ assessments, the findings indicate an overall intermediate level of methodological competence, with variation across individual components of teaching practice. The lowest scores were observed for the expository teaching method and the application of functional tasks, whereas higher scores were recorded for communication with students and the use of teaching resources. title: Beyond the Screen: A Hyper-Interactive Video and Hands-On Framework for Inclusive Elementary Physics with Autistic Learners (ASD Level 1)
abstract: Inclusive elementary physics education for autistic learners (ASD Level 1) requires structured, predictable, and multimodal environments that support conceptual understanding and collaborative inquiry. This study evaluates a hyper-interactive framework that combines interactive video, hands-on experimentation, and peer collaboration. Thirty-six fifth- and sixth-grade students (24 with ASD Level 1 and 12 typically developing) participated in two units, Electricity and Mechanics. Across the two phases, autistic learners experienced both ASD–ASD and ASD–TD pairing conditions, whereas TD participants remained in ASD–TD pairs. In Electricity, pairing was based on students’ verbal and intellectual levels; in Mechanics, these criteria were retained and domain-specific Mechanics performance was additionally considered. title: Integrating Career Development Learning with Work-Integrated Learning: A Multiple Case Study Advancing Education for Sustainable Development
abstract: Engaging in work-integrated learning (WIL) activities helps students develop critical skills, formulate their professional identities, and refine their career direction. Integrating career development learning (CDL) and WIL throughout a degree is a mechanism for fostering sustainability. This multiple case study explores individual and institutional practices that enable integration of CDL with WIL. Data include interviews with careers and WIL practitioners at seven institutions in three countries. The findings indicate that clear communication via policy guidance, across teams and through information systems, facilitates integration of CDL and WIL in the curriculum. Integrating CDL with WIL can make iterative WIL experiences accessible in contexts where students have lower access to workplace-based WIL. Integrated CDL and WIL can raise awareness and develop sustainability-related skills, such as ethical reasoning, diversity awareness, ability to work in interdisciplinary teams, and complex problem-solving. title: A Clinical SEL Intervention for Pupils in Inclusive Education
abstract: Preparing educators for teaching in inclusive education settings presents both conceptual and practical challenges. This study examines the implementation process of a professional development (PD) programme designed to equip teachers with Social and Emotional Learning (SEL) strategies tailored for pupils in inclusive classrooms. We analysed comprehensive reports submitted by 21 teachers who attended the PD programme and learned a structured intervention protocol, which enabled them to develop customised SEL interventions for individual pupils. Content analysis revealed that while the interventions were highly individualised to reflect the distinct characteristics and challenges of the pupils, they shared common intervention practices. Specifically, the analysis identified six primary intervention strategies; however, not all strategies were applied in each case or in the same temporal sequence. These findings underscore the feasibility of equipping educators with targeted SEL tools, offering valuable insights for advancing pedagogical practices in inclusive settings.

title: What Do Educators Need to Implement STEAM Education? A Systematic Review
abstract: Implementing STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics) education places substantial, varied demands on teachers, yet evidence on what educators need to enact it remains fragmented. This systematic review synthesizes empirical research on educators’ needs for STEAM implementation across five interrelated dimensions—preparation, implementation, coordination, collaboration, and professional development—as outlined in the STEAMCompEdu framework. A systematic search of Scopus, Web of Science, ERIC, and Wiley Online Library, reported per PRISMA 2020, identified 62 eligible peer-reviewed studies from 29 single-country contexts and 7 multi-country studies (2019–July 2026) and synthesized them through combined deductive and inductive coding. title: Student Teachers’ Metacognitive Awareness and Perceptions of Problem-Solving Ability
abstract: Metacognitive awareness, defined as the ability to plan, monitor, and evaluate one’s own learning, plays a crucial role in problem solving. It enables individuals to determine not only which strategies to use but also when and how to apply them effectively. This study aimed to examine the relationship between student teachers’ metacognitive awareness levels and their perceptions of problem-solving ability. A descriptive survey design was employed. Participants were selected through convenience and purposive sampling, comprising 200 student teachers: 100 from special education (60 females, 40 males) and 100 from preschool education (75 females, 25 males). Data were collected using the Personal Information Form, Problem Solving Inventory, and Metacognitive Awareness Inventory. The findings showed that pre-service teachers had high levels of perceived problem-solving skills and metacognitive awareness. title: Exploratory Pilot Case Study on Compassionate Leadership Training as an Upstream Measure to Address Workplace Stress in School Leaders
abstract: Prior research on compassion fatigue and burnout has suggested that understanding and developing compassion and self-compassion has positive effects on mental health. At present in Alberta, Canada, few education programs integrate information about how to become a compassionate leader in teacher or school leader training, despite this mission being highly valued across school jurisdictions. This exploratory pilot study focused on the short- and longer-term influence of providing compassionate leadership training with one group of teachers and school leaders (n = 30) over a six-month period. The guiding question for this research study was as follows: What is the influence of integrating compassionate leadership training on teachers’ and school leaders’ practices directly following and six months after receiving training? Quantitative data were collected via pre- and post-training online surveys, and qualitative interviews (n = 9) were held with volunteers six months after the completion of the intervention. title: Who Discloses Disability in Land-Based Higher Education—And What Happens After Graduation? A Sector-Level Analysis
abstract: Disability disclosure has implications for student experience and graduate outcomes, yet little is known about disclosure in land-based higher education, a sector with distinctive vocational and practical provision. Using aggregated Higher Education Statistics Agency data on first-year enrolments (2015/16–2024/25; 88,430 full-person equivalents [FPEs]) and the Graduate Outcomes Survey (academic years 2017/18–2022/23; 31,275 FPEs eligible graduates, of whom 17,840 FPEs responded), this study examined disclosure patterns and their association with student characteristics and graduate employment, using design-based chi-squared tests and logistic regression with standard errors clustered by provider. Disclosure increased over the period (unadjusted OR for 2024/25 vs. 2015/16 = 2.30, 95% CI 1.92–2.77). title: Neurodiversity-Affirmative Model, Social Camouflaging, and Psychological Well-Being of Neurodivergent Students in Inclusive Contexts: A Systematic Review
abstract: Although the enrollment of neurodivergent students is increasing globally, persistent normative educational environments force these students to socially camouflage, which severely impairs their psychological well-being. This systematic review synthesizes empirical evidence on the associations between educational practices based on the Neurodiversity-Affirmative Model, social camouflaging, and psychological well-being within inclusive contexts. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines and the PICOS framework, 37 empirical studies published between 2015 and 2026 were identified across five major databases (WoS, PubMed, ERIC, APA PsycINFO, Scopus) and evaluated using the MMAT tool. title: Mapping the Intellectual and Thematic Evolution of L2 Willingness to Communicate Research: A Bibliometric Analysis
abstract: Willingness to communicate (WTC) in a second language (L2) is a central construct in second language acquisition (SLA), yet the intellectual structure and thematic development of the field remain insufficiently mapped. This study provides a bibliometric analysis of 477 English-language L2 WTC records indexed in the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) from 1996 to 31 July 2025. Using CiteSpace (6.4.R1), the study examines publication trends, collaboration networks, co-citation structures, keyword co-occurrence, thematic evolution, and research bursts. The findings show sustained growth in L2 WTC research and a knowledge base anchored in established work on psychological and affective dimensions, including anxiety, motivation, attitudes, confidence, and emotions. Collaboration networks indicate that research activity is concentrated among a relatively limited set of countries and institutions, while co-citation analysis reveals a highly structured intellectual base centered on influential work in WTC, emotions, classroom environments, and related psychological and contextual dimensions. abstract: The single-quantum double-slit experiment is often taught through a compact narrative of localised detections, interference, and wave–particle duality that may conceal weak explanatory coordination.
